annotations.text:
PAPER & INK — both modes

The character comes from SHAPE, not light: a 2px outline and a hard offset shadow, so every card reads as a physical piece on a table.

That is exactly why it inverts cleanly. Flip the ground and the ink, keep the geometry, and it is the same design at night — not a second design to maintain.

TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY DO NOT FLIP

1. The six prisoner colours. They are the game's signal. If a match looked different at night, the one rule of the game would change with the time of day.

2. The geometry. Same radii, same 2px line, same 4px drop, both modes.

BOTH MODES COME FROM ONE DRAWING

Each screen is written once with token names and emitted twice — see _build.py and _tokens.md beside these files.

Hand-drawing the second set is how a dark mode drifts: someone nudges a radius in light, forgets the dark file, and six months later they are two designs.

NOT SHOWN: the battle screen.

Its chrome is only the two score pills and a hint line — the screen is almost entirely the 3D board, which does not change with the theme.

Worth deciding: does the theme follow the phone's own light/dark setting, or is it a switch in Settings? I would follow the phone and offer an override.
